title.en: Gravitation, mass, weight and apparent weight

text.en: Newton wondered why an apple falls to the ground but the Moon does not fall onto the Earth. He realised that the same pull, gravitation, acts on both, and that this pull depends on the masses and the distance between them.

Newton's universal law of gravitation says that every particle of matter attracts every other particle with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres.
In symbols F = G m1 m2 / r squared, where G is the universal gravitational constant, 6.674 times 10 to the power minus 11 N m squared per kg squared.
The force is always attractive, acts along the line joining the masses and does not depend on the medium between them.
For a body of mass m on the Earth the force is G M m / R squared, and by Newton's second law it is also m g, so g = G M / R squared.
The mean value of g on the Earth is 9.8 metre per second squared, which means a freely falling body gains 9.8 m/s of velocity every second.
Since g depends on the radius, it is greatest at the poles, least at the equator, decreases with height and depth and is zero at the centre of the Earth.
From g, R and G we can find the mass of the Earth, M = g R squared / G, which is about 5.972 times 10 to the power 24 kilogram.
Mass is the quantity of matter and never changes; weight is the gravitational force W = m g, a vector pointing towards the centre of the Earth, measured in newton.
A 60 kg person weighs 588 N on the Earth but only 97.5 N on the Moon, where g is 1.625, while the mass stays 60 kg.
Apparent weight is the reaction force R of the surface: in a lift it is mg at rest, m(g + a) when accelerating upwards, m(g - a) when accelerating downwards and zero in free fall, which we call weightlessness.

problem.en: A person of mass 60 kg stands in a lift. Find the apparent weight when the lift accelerates upwards at 2 m/s2 and downwards at 2 m/s2. Take g = 9.8 m/s2.

text.en: Weight at rest is mg = 60 x 9.8 = 588 N.
Upward acceleration: R = m(g + a) = 60 x (9.8 + 2) = 708 N.

why.en: The floor pushes harder, so he feels heavier.

text.en: Downward acceleration: R = m(g - a) = 60 x (9.8 - 2) = 468 N.

why.en: The floor pushes less, so he feels lighter.

text.en: If the cable breaks, a = g and R = 60 x (9.8 - 9.8) = 0, so he is weightless.

prompt.en: Explain the difference between mass and weight and why a person feels lighter when a lift starts to move down.

requiredIdeas.en: Mass is the quantity of matter and is constant, weight is the force mg and changes with g
Apparent weight is the reaction R of the floor
When the lift accelerates down R = m(g - a), which is less than mg

commonMisconceptions.en: Mass and weight are the same thing
Weight is zero on the Moon

points.en: F = G m1 m2 / r squared and g = G M / R squared.
g is 9.8 m/s2 on Earth and 1.625 m/s2 on the Moon.
Mass is constant; weight = mg changes with place.
Apparent weight R = m(g + a) going up and m(g - a) coming down; free fall gives weightlessness.
